summary: This is a clean restack of two shape-disjoint, already-measured changes. diff master vs a_merged.py is exactly the parent's two config-only edits (sliding gate widened to every batch at q_len 1, splits = 16 for decode), and both parents passed 16/16 with this exact sliding code and master's full-layer code. Expect about +1.4% headline (~1.366x), mostly from sliding decode_16. That is near the CI edge, but it is safe for a scored submit.
justification: The mechanism is already measured, not just inferred. In job 179dd013d3a347e4, sliding decode_16 went from 20.8 to 15.5 us (_sliding_fused_kernel 12.8 us vs FA3 9.9 + combine 3.3 + prepare 1.8 + pre-attn 1.7 + norm) and sliding decode_32 from 25.2 to 24.7 us (22.1 us kernel). decode_1 stayed byte-identical (_num_splits(1,2) == 16). Verify and full shapes were untouched. The merge leaves master's CUDA split-KV path (window == 0 only) and all of the q_len 8 FA3 path alone, so the per-shape expectations are consistent. Load arithmetic (TASK.md weights 46/16): decode_16 load goes from 46*20.8 + 16*123.0 = 2925 us to ~2681 us (~1.09x on that load). The decode_32 load is ~1.00-1.01x. The geomean over 6 loads is ~1.015x, so the headline is ~1.366x vs best 1.3468 [1.3266, 1.3670]. The CI low will probably still overlap best's CI high, so expect 'neutral/unproven-vs-best' again. Judge it per shape, as with the decode1-gate merge-by-hand precedent in DECISIONS.md. Weakest link: the decode_32 'faster' claim. The fused kernel at B=32 (1024 CTAs) costs 22.1 us of kernel time against FA3's 13.2 us main kernel. The shape gain was only ~2%, which is inside the ~1.5-2.5% per-shape drift in LESSONS, so decode_32 should be expected flat and could read slightly slower. The design is far from its floor at B=32 (3.3 us SoL): the serial tile count is no longer the limiter there, and occupancy or combine cost probably is. Master has not made this moot: the incumbent sliding decode_16/32 path is still FA3 (FINDINGS profile).
confounders: full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv: no confound. Its gate requires window == 0, and the sliding gate requires window != 0. The CUDA path uses its own workspace (no _COUNTERS), and its import-time self-check calls kernel_fn only on window-0 synthetic data, so the widened sliding gate never sees it. The full rows' numbers come from master's code, so only sliding decode_16/32 should move.
sliding-fused-triton-decode1-gate: this is the code being widened, not a confounder. B=1 keeps S=16 and the same predicate result, so decode_1 is byte-identical.

fused-preattention-triton: on sliding decode_16/32 its _pre_attention_kernel launch is removed (the fused kernel does norm/rope/cache store itself). That is part of the measured gain, not an interaction. Full and verify use it unchanged.
fa3-hdim128-head-pairing / paired-heads-launch-cleanup / -ab-tune-batch-gate: full layers only (window == 0), so they share no launch, memory traffic or numerics with the sliding decode path.
interference: No companion is needed. Each sub-change has already been isolated: the gate widened at _num_splits depth (sliding-single-launch-fused-attention: 23.9/38.5 us), S=16 at every batch (parent: 15.5/24.7 us), and the CUDA full path (master: 123.0/257.7 us). The shapes are disjoint, so the per-shape rows attribute any change directly. A gain or a loss on the sliding decode rows can only come from the two merged lines, and full/verify rows act as in-run controls against drift. If decode_32 reads slower, the follow-up is a stacked ab-tune (gate the fused kernel to batch <= 16 so B=32 returns to FA3, or S=32 at B=32), not a companion now. Checks are spent anyway.
open_questions: decode_32: is the fused kernel at B=32 (22.1 us vs FA3 main 13.2 us) worth keeping? If the scored run shows sliding decode_32 at or below master's 25.2 us within drift, consider a follow-up that gates the fused path to batch <= 16, or tries S=32 at B=32.

Harvest: read the log tail for '[splitkv] load_inline compiled' and three self-check lines. A '[splitkv] SELF-CHECK FAILED' or load_inline failure would mean the full rows measured the FA3 fallback, which would muddle the headline but not the sliding rows.

Compile budget: CUDA load_inline (~41 s) plus the Triton fused-kernel variants (PAGE 1/64, ROPE on, S=16) are the same set as the two parents compiled separately, which should be well inside 15 minutes.
